brief: The FOMC hiked 25bp to 3.75-4% on September 16, a meeting Goldman calls more hawkish than expected: a 16-2 majority projected at least one more 2026 hike (four participants wanted two), no dissents against the hike, the median dot stayed elevated at 3.5-3.75% through 2029, the neutral-rate dot rose to 3.25% (above Goldman's own 3.19% forecast), and Chairman Warsh called the hike a removal of a dose of accommodation three times without giving a neutral-rate estimate. Goldman now expects a second 25bp hike in October, reversing its prior call that September would be the only hike, because consecutive-meeting hikes better fit the FOMC's stated aim of a timelier return to 2% than an every-other-meeting pace. Its terminal-rate forecast stays 3.25-3.5%, now reached via an added March 2028 cut. The elevated 2029 dot is an upside risk, possibly reflecting AI-driven investment demand or just a signaling choice. Market-implied hike odds rose to 51% for October and 78% for December. Goldman sees the November midterms as less of an obstacle to a second hike than to an initial one; further hikes beyond October are possible but not its base case, since its core PCE forecast runs below the FOMC median.
